title: Coefficients of the reverse characteristic polynomial

source.place: node def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family, order 2856, last sentence: 'It has constant coefficient $1$, degree $\dim_{\Ql}V_{i,\ell}$, and leading coefficient $(-1)^{\dim V_{i,\ell}}\det(F_{i,\ell})$' (the same claim is made in literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-trace-formula/sk-def-frobmod/def-zl-frobenius-trace-series.md)

proof.text: Step 1: $P$ is the reverse of the characteristic polynomial. Let $\chi_F(T)=\det(T-F\mid V)\in K[T]$ be the characteristic polynomial of $F$ [def-weil-characteristic-polynomial]. By [lem-weil-reverse-charpoly-eq-reverse], $P(T)=\det(1-TF\mid V)=\operatorname{rev}(\chi_F)(T)$, the reverse of $\chi_F$ [def-weil-reverse-polynomial] taken with respect to $\deg\chi_F$.

proof.text: Step 2: the two coefficients of $\chi_F$ that matter. Write $\chi_F(T)=\sum_{k\ge0}a_kT^k$ with $a_k=[T^k]\chi_F\in K$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]. By [lem-weil-charpoly-monic-degree], $\chi_F$ is monic of degree $n$: $\deg\chi_F=n$, $a_n=1$ and $a_k=0$ for $k>n$. By [lem-weil-charpoly-constant-coefficient-det], $\det(F\mid V)=(-1)^na_0$ [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]; multiplying by $(-1)^n$ and using $((-1)^n)^2=1$ gives $a_0=(-1)^n\det(F\mid V)$. (For $n=0$: $\chi_F=1$, $a_0=1=\det(F\mid 0)$, consistent.)

proof.text: Step 3: the coefficients of $P$. Since $\deg\chi_F=n$ (Step 2), [lem-weil-reverse-polynomial-coefficients] applied to $f=\chi_F$, $d=n$, together with Step 1, gives $[T^j]P=a_{n-j}$ for $0\le j\le n$ and $[T^j]P=0$ for $j>n$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient].

proof.text: Step 4: claim 1. By Step 3 with $j=0$ and Step 2, the constant coefficient of $P$ is $P(0)=[T^0]P=a_n=1$. In particular $P\neq0$. (Directly: $P(0)=\det(1-0\cdot F\mid V)=\det(1_V)=1$; in Mathlib this is `Matrix.eval_charpolyRev`.)

proof.text: Step 5: claim 2. By Step 3, $[T^j]P=0$ for every $j>n$, so $\deg P\le n$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient]; and by Step 3 with $j=n$ and Step 2, $[T^n]P=a_0=(-1)^n\det(F\mid V)$.
